To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) high fat feeding induces insulin resistance, 2) hexosamine flux is elevated in high fat fed mice, 3) hexosamine overexpression in muscle induces insulin resistance, and 4) high fat feeding and hexosamines are additive in inducing insulin sensitivity in muscle.
hexosamine synthesis mediates the effects of both carbohydrate and fatty acid excess on insulin resistance.

1) high fat feeding and transgenic expression of glutamine:fructosamine-6-phosphate transaminase (GFAT), the rate-limiting step in hexosamine synthesis are not additive in their ability to induce insulin resistance, and 2) the effects of high fat feeding and GFAT overexpression on leptin secretion are also not additive, suggesting a common pathway for these two stimuli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms by which nutrients regulate glucose metabolism, and how these processes are perturbed in the pathogenesis and progression of diabetes.
the molecular basis for insulin resistance, a key feature of type 2 (non-insulin dependent) diabetes, which is a major health problem.
the role of the hexosamines as mediators of nutrient sensing and the induction of insulin resistance.

high fat diet and hexosamine pathway are not additive in causing insulin resistance.

the hexosamine biosynthesis pathway is a common nutrient sensing pathway and that the flux of glucose or fat through this pathway is a common mechanism by which glucose and fat induce insulin resistance.
hexosamine flux and fat feeding do not act additively, but rather in a common pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hexosamine biosynthesis pathway (HBP) is the key nutrient sensing pathway that is responsible for the induction of insulin resistance.
the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway (HBP) is a key nutrient-sensing pathway that links nutrient fluxes to the development of insulin resistance.
hexosamine pathway activation is a major mechanism by which both glucose and lipids cause insulin resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
high fat feeding and increased hexosamine pathway activity have a similar effect on insulin action and that the effects are not additive.
high fat diets do not increase insulin resistance in mice that already have insulin resistance due to hexosamine overproduction.
high fat feeding is not additive with increased hexosamine flux in inducing insulin resistance, and that the two may share a common fuel sensing pathway.
